question.problem: Suppose that $A$ and $B$ are two events such that $P(A)=0.45,$ $P(B)=0.35,$ and $P(A\cap B)=0.3,$ find $P(A\cup B).$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14284903/assets/35e807b7de787f50d0cbff770e4083cef84b4d35030b4c506b1db5646cf7a358.png)

The addition law for probability states that

$$
P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B).
$$

So, to calculate $P(A\cup B),$ we apply the addition law:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A\cup B) & =P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B) \\  & =0.45+0.35-0.3 \\  & =0.5\end{aligned}
$$
